title: Let an agent decide which emails you can ignore
summary: A developer built an agent that sorts email and parks the least urgent fifth on a 7-day timer; on test mail, she reports about 85% of parked emails truly got no reply.
agent_role: The agent scores each email, writes summaries for urgent ones, and waits on parked ones, escalating if the sender writes again or archiving after seven days; the human reads the morning digest.
outcome: Author reports about 1 in 10 emails can be parked with 92-93% accuracy, missing about 2.5% of mail that got a reply.
what_they_did: The developer built an agent that scores each email by how costly ignoring it would be. The top fifth get a short summary from a local model for a morning digest. The bottom fifth are parked. If the sender follows up within a week, the email comes back. If not, it is archived. She tested it on a public mailbox of old company emails.
how_it_went: She reports that on 1,981 test emails, 398 were parked and about 85% truly got no reply. In a small demo, 7 of 8 parked emails were archived correctly and 1 came back after a follow-up.
worth_knowing: The local model first summarized the oldest forwarded message instead of the new reply. Cutting each email at the forwarding marker fixed it.
prompt: Help me build a lazy email assistant for [my email account]. Look at my past emails and replies to learn which messages I usually answer. Sort new mail into three groups: needs me, low priority, and probably ignorable. For 'needs me', write a two-line summary and a suggested action in a morning digest. For ignorable mail, wait [7] days; bring it back if the sender writes again. Show me the sorting for the first week, and do not archive or delete anything until I approve.

curation.rationale: A carefully tested email agent that decides which mail can be ignored, with code, real numbers and honest limits; a fresh angle on email triage.
